[[File:Example_of_the_Multicover_Bifiltration.webp|thumb|upright=1.2|The 2- and 3-fold covers of 7 points in the plane with respect to a particular scale parameter.]]
The '''multicover bifiltration''' is a two-parameter sequence of nested [[Topological space|topological spaces]] derived from the covering of a [[finite set]] in a [[metric space]] by growing [[Ball (mathematics)|metric balls]]. It is a multidimensional extension of the [[Offset Filtration|offset filtration]] that captures density information about the underlying data set by filtering the points of the offsets at each index according to how many balls cover each point.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Botnan |first1=Magnus Bakke |last2=Lesnick |first2=Michael |date=2022 |title=An Introduction to Multiparameter Persistence |pages=26 |class=math.AT |eprint=2203.14289}}</ref> The multicover bifiltration has been an object of study within multidimensional [[persistent homology]] and [[topological data analysis]].<ref == Definition ==
Following the notation of Corbet et al. (2022), given a finite set <math>A\subset \mathbb R^d</math>, the '''multicover bifiltration''' on <math>A</math> is a two-parameter filtration indexed by <math>\mathbb R \times \mathbb N^{\text{op}}</math> defined index-wise as <math>\operatorname{Cov}_{r,k} := \{b \in \mathbb R^d : ||b-a|| \leq r \text{ for at least } k \text{ points } a\in A\}</math>, where <math>\mathbb N</math> denotes the non-negative integers.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Corbet |first1=René |last2=Kerber |first2=Michael |last3=Lesnick |first3=Michael |last4=Osang |first4=Georg |date=2023-02-20 |title=Computing the Multicover Bifiltration |journal=Discrete & Computational Geometry |volume=70 |issue=2 |pages=376–405 |language=en |doi=10.1007/s00454-022-00476-8 |pmid=37581017 |pmc=10423148 |issn=0179-5376|arxiv=2103.07823 }}</ref> Note that when <math>k=1</math> is fixed we recover the [[Offset Filtration]].

== Properties ==
The multicover bifiltration admits a topologically equivalent polytopal model of polynomial size, called the "[[rhomboid]] bifiltration."<ref name=":2" /> The rhomboid bifiltration is an extension of the rhomboid [[Tiling (geometry)|tiling]] introduced by Edelsbrunner and Osang in 2021 for computing the [[persistent homology]] of the multicover bifiltration along one axis of the indexing set.<ref name=":0" /> The rhomboid bifiltration on a set of <math>n</math> points in a [[Euclidean space]] can be computed in polynomial time.<ref name=":2" />

[[File:Rhomboid_Tiling.webp|thumb|An example of the rhomboid tiling on a set of five points.]]

The multicover bifiltration is also topologically equivalent to a multicover nerve construction due to Sheehy called the [[Subdivision bifiltration|subdivision-Čech bifiltration]], which considers the [[barycentric subdivision]] on the nerve of the offsets.<ref>D. R. Sheehy, “[https://donsheehy.net/sheehy12multicover.html A multicover nerve for geometric inference],” in ''CCCG: Canadian conference in computational geometry'', 2012.
</ref> In particular, the subdivision-Čech and multicover bifiltrations are [[Weak equivalence (homotopy theory)|weakly equivalent]], and hence have [[Isomorphism|isomorphic]] [[Homology (mathematics)|homology]] modules in all dimensions.<ref name=":1" /> However, the subdivision-Čech bifiltration has an exponential number of simplices in the size of the data set, and hence is not amenable to efficient direct computations.<ref name=":2" />
